variables.name: Air temperature (2 m)
variables.description: Annual mean of daily mean 2 m air temperature.
variables.region_unsupported_reason: NASA POWER is served here as daily point time series for one grid cell; a region-wide statistic would require many cells and is not implemented.

variables.name: Relative humidity (2 m)
variables.description: Annual mean of daily 2 m relative humidity.
variables.region_unsupported_reason: NASA POWER is served here as daily point time series for one grid cell; region-wide analysis is not implemented.

variables.name: Extreme heat frequency
variables.description: Share of days whose maximum temperature exceeds the local 1991–2020 calendar-day 90th percentile (bootstrap-adjusted inside the reference period).
variables.annual_value: percentage of valid days above the local 90th-percentile threshold
variables.region_unsupported_reason: Thresholds are local to one NASA POWER grid cell; a regional exceedance statistic is not implemented.

variables.name: Precipitation
variables.description: Annual total precipitation from twelve monthly accumulations.
variables.region_unsupported_reason: Region-wide IMERG analysis (area-weighted, mask-aware) is planned but not yet implemented; point analysis uses the native 0.1° cell.

variables.name: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
variables.description: Annual mean of quality-filtered MODIS NDVI averaged over a circular area.
variables.annual_value: equal-weight mean of monthly means of quality-filtered 16-day composites
variables.spatial_resolution: 250 m pixels averaged over a circle (radius_km)

variables.name: Soil moisture
variables.description: Monthly soil moisture from one dataset at a time: GLDAS-2.1 Noah 0–10 cm model layer, or SMAP L3 Enhanced (≈0–5 cm satellite retrieval), version 005 or 006.
variables.annual_value: equal-weight mean of 12 usable monthly means
variables.region_unsupported_reason: Soil moisture uses the native grid cell containing the point; region-wide analysis is not implemented.

caveats: Mann-Kendall significance is reported only after a lag-1 serial-dependence screen. An independent Monte Carlo check (5,000 replications) found that this screened test can reject a true no-trend hypothesis more often than the nominal 5% when annual values are autocorrelated (about 10.5% at n = 45, lag-1 autocorrelation 0.3). Treat 'statistically significant' as indicative, not as a guaranteed 5% false-positive rate.
